items.label: KLA Q4 FY2026 (07-28-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL — HBM PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY 'RIVALS ADVANCED LOGIC'

set.signal: CALL — HBM PROCESS-CONTROL INTENSITY 'RIVALS ADVANCED LOGIC': CFO Bren Higgins said high-bandwidth memory 'from an intensity point of view is a unique animal for KLA' (more customization in the base die, the integration of each DRAM, the ultimate value, performance specs) and that across some products 'we're seeing intensity levels that are rivaling what we see in advanced logic'; conventional DRAM intensity has improved, but 'conventional DRAM isn't the same as high-bandwidth memory DRAM in terms of its process control intensity'. 2027 memory setup (CFO): in DRAM 'the greenfield opportunity and the retooling of those fabs creates a new opportunity'; 'you can imagine that where prices are and how that translates into margins, that the value of yield is pretty high'; increasing EUV adoption in DRAM is raising process control intensity; 'You will also see some greenfield investment in flash. While flash isn't our strongest market', it should create some opportunities. Mix: September quarter memory approximately 27% of semiconductor process control systems revenue to semiconductor customers (DRAM approximately 90%, NAND 10%); CFO: 'I do expect memory to be a bigger percentage in the December quarter and likely to remain there through the first half of the year.' Cost side (CFO): the memory-pricing gross-margin impact was 'somewhere around 100 basis points. It's probably a little bit more than that, and I think that likely continues as we move forward through 2027'; 'I would expect you start to see some normalization on the pricing front that moves from a headwind to a tailwind.'
set.figure: HBM PC intensity rivals advanced logic on some products; memory GM headwind ~100bps or a bit more, likely continues through 2027

items.reason: Quotes were paraphrased inside quote marks and hedges dropped ('likely continues', 'likely to remain'); rewritten with the verbatim words.
items.evidence: I do expect memory to be a bigger percentage in the December quarter and likely to remain there through the first half of the year.

items.label: KLA Q4 FY2026 (07-28-2026)
items.signal_prefix: FISCAL Q4 (June quarter) and FY2026 close

set.signal: FISCAL Q4 (June quarter) and FY2026 close: total revenues $3.66B, ABOVE the midpoint of guidance; GAAP net income $1.36B with GAAP diluted EPS $1.04 and non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.05, both at the UPPER END of the guidance range. Full fiscal year 2026: revenues $13.58B with GAAP net income $4.83B and GAAP diluted EPS $3.66. By segment, SEMICONDUCTOR PROCESS CONTROL — the core franchise — delivered $3.257B in the quarter (up 13% from $2.878B a year earlier) and $12.245B for the fiscal year (up 12% from $10.947B); Specialty Semiconductor Process $159.7M in the quarter ($584.1M for the year); PCB and Component Inspection $241.1M in the quarter, up 56% from $154.1M, and $750.4M for the year versus $621.7M. GUIDANCE FOR FISCAL Q1 2027 (September quarter) STEPS UP TO $4.0 BILLION +/- $200M, with GAAP gross margin 61.6% +/-1.0%, non-GAAP gross margin 62.5% +/-1.0%, and GAAP diluted EPS $1.14 +/- $0.10.

items.reason: 'roughly +9% sequentially' is the enricher's own arithmetic, stated by no source.
items.evidence: KLA September quarter guidance is for revenue of $4 billion ± $200 million.

items.label: KLA Q4 FY2026 (07-28-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL — WFE RAISED AGAIN AND THE 2027 SETUP

set.signal: CALL — WFE RAISED AGAIN AND THE 2027 SETUP: CFO Bren Higgins raised the CY2026 wafer equipment market expectation, including advanced packaging, to 'approximately the low $150 billion range' (from $140 billion-plus), mid-20% growth above the approximate $120 billion level in 2025, and said 'Given the unprecedented visibility from customers, we continue to plan for significant growth in calendar 2027'. CY2027 (CFO): 'there's a consensus view out there, I would say, that's somewhere in and around the $190 billion range' with 'not too many bearish views'; '$190 billion or so translates into a mid-20 type growth rate, which is similar to the growth rate in 2026'; KLA is 'driving the company to ensure that we can supply and support the more bullish views', running scenarios such as 'what if demand was 10% higher? What if 20% was higher?'. Supply (CFO): KLA has been 'meeting with some of our critical suppliers and planning and doing capacity agreements for our needs, we believe in the 2029 and beyond time-frame' for optical components ('We're actively engaging in those discussions now'), where 'it can take 12 to 24 months to put New capacity in place'. Demand proof (CFO): 'We'd expect that the RPO, or backlog, would be about $12.5 billion' in the coming 10-Q, expected to keep growing with the order funnel; lead times 'in about the 12-month range', 'closer to 18 to 24 months' on certain products, with customer conversations 'about deliveries really in the second half of 2027'; second-half CY2026 growth over the first half 'approximately 20%' as capacity comes online in long lead time supply chain areas (first-half shipments were held back by shortages of longer lead time materials), with continued sequential growth into 2027. Broadening leading edge, CEO Rick Wallace: 'the world needs more advanced logic. There was a desire by many customers to broaden the other players outside of the leader'; 'The broadening has really been happening as we hoped it would'; CFO: new fabs and 'a lot of greenfield activity' add demand for new tools. Other (CFO): incremental operating margin 59% in the quarter; services on a new 13% to 15% long-term growth model.
set.figure: CY26 WFE low-$150B range (raised from $140B+); CFO cites ~$190B 2027 consensus; RPO expected ~$12.5B; second half ~20% above first half; supplier capacity agreements for 2029 and beyond under discussion

items.reason: Removed analyst content (the 4-raises count, Intel 14A / Samsung-Broadcom / Rapidus / Terafab examples, the $215B / $1.4T 2030 figures and 'semi revenue likely hits $1.4T' are from analyst questions), the outside 'matching Lam's view' note, and 'already being overtaken' (CEO: no position to reset 2030); supplier agreements are 'actively engaging in those discussions', not signed.
items.evidence: We're still a long way. We only had our Investor Day in March, and here we are in July, so we're in no position to reset anything as it pertains to 2030.

items.label: KLA Q4 FY2026 (07-28-2026)

set.signal: CALL — ADVANCED-PACKAGING OUTLOOK RAISED AGAIN: advanced-packaging process-control systems revenue now expected at ~$1.1 BILLION in CY2026, UP MORE THAN 70% YoY — raised from the prior high-50s% growth view, and ~2x THE MARKET's growth. KLA's view of the advanced-packaging equipment MARKET itself accelerated from ~20% growth at the start of the year to MID-TO-HIGH 30s% for 2026. Drivers: accelerated share and adoption of FRONT-END-designed inspection/metrology systems pulled into packaging by customers (long-awaited SOIC and HYBRID BONDING needs now arriving, DIE-TO-WAFER bonding next) — largely leveraging the existing portfolio, so modest incremental R&D; packaging is shorter-lead-time business, so it inflects fast. The Orbotech thesis is compounding: combined specialty-semi + PCB businesses to grow >25% in CY2026, with CFO Bren Higgins saying the long-term growth rate is 'likely somewhere in the high single-digit range, and we'll see over several years whether there's a structural growth element that materializes' as high-performance computing changes a business 'historically more capacity-centric and tied to mobility' — 'the value of those boards is much higher... I wish I could ship more.'
set.figure: Adv-packaging PC revenue raised to ~$1.1B CY26 (+>70%, ~2x market); market view up to mid-high-30s% growth; PCB LT growth 'likely' high single digits

items.reason: 'from mid-to-high' was the analyst's recollection of the Investor Day figure; the CFO's high-single-digit view is hedged ('likely', 'we'll see').
items.evidence: I would say it's likely somewhere in the high single-digit range, and we'll see over several years whether there's a structural growth element that materializes
